caption: A wooden snap-trap base rests on a dark textured mat before a reddish brick wall, its copper kill-bar lying flat across the board. Balanced atop the bar's wire loop is a smaller wooden lever tipped with a yellow clip, propped at an upward angle. At the left edge a person's fingers appear briefly, then withdraw and leave the frame within the first moments. As the hand disappears, the small lever slowly descends, its raised yellow end tilting downward toward a near-horizontal position. The trap base itself stays fixed on the surface throughout. Over the latter portion of the clip the copper kill-bar gradually swings upward from its flat position, rising into a tall, near-vertical orientation. These rotations proceed slowly and continuously, with no sudden snap or impact visible. The brick background and mat texture remain unchanged as the mechanism reconfigures.
relations: As the hand withdraws, the yellow-tipped lever tilts downward from its propped angle.
The copper kill-bar slowly swings upward from the board toward a vertical orientation.
The wooden base stays fixed on the mat while the attached components rotate.
